title: Design System: Pidzoom Portable charger HW178P

title.purpose: Product identity in the fixed header only.

motion.name: state-only
motion.purpose: Immediate hover, focus, and status feedback only.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single ordinary next action, calm and explicit.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background:#00726B; color:#fff; min-height:30px; padding:2px 12px; border:1px solid #00544E; border-radius:4px; font:650 13px system-ui; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#00544E; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #00726B; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: State-aware Output Control
components.description: One fixed header location: Start for fresh explicit OFF, immediate Stop for fresh explicit ON, disabled otherwise.
components.css: .ds-btn-stop { background:#BE241F; color:#fff; min-height:38px; padding:2px 18px; border:1px solid #8D1714; border-radius:4px; font:750 13px system-ui; } .ds-btn-stop:hover { background:#9E1D19; } .ds-btn-stop:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #00726B; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Symbol plus text keeps state independent from color.
components.css: .ds-status { display:inline-block; background:#E4F4F1; color:#00544E; border:1px solid #00726B; border-radius:4px; padding:5px 8px; font:650 13px system-ui; }

components.name: Target Field
components.description: Exact value, unit, and configured range stay together.
components.css: .ds-field { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; color:#101A1C; font:13px system-ui; } .ds-field input { width:82px; min-height:30px; padding:1px 8px; border:1px solid #C4CCCE; border-radius:4px; font:13px 'SF Mono',monospace; } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #00726B; outline-offset:1px; } .ds-field span { color:#516164; }

components.name: Telemetry Reading
components.description: Stable label, aligned number, and fixed engineering unit.
components.css: .ds-reading { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr auto 28px; gap:6px; align-items:end; padding:7px 8px; background:#fff; color:#101A1C; } .ds-reading span { grid-column:1 / -1; color:#516164; font:13px system-ui; } .ds-reading strong { font:650 25px/1.15 'SF Mono',monospace; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-reading em { color:#516164; font:normal 13px system-ui; }

narrative.overview: The interface is a light, high-contrast work surface for an engineer operating high-voltage equipment in mixed bench lighting. Information is aligned, measured, and explicit; the application earns trust by showing connection, authentication, freshness, provenance, and uncertainty instead of polishing those details away. The 1220×800 default window uses a fixed header, a stable workbench, and tabs for transport evidence. It stays usable down to 1100×720 without fluid display type or decorative rearrangement.
keyCharacteristics: Pure-white working canvas and cool neutral instrument panels.
One restrained teal identity color and sparse semantic signals.
Large tabular numeric telemetry with compact engineering units.
Persistent textual status, safety interlocks, and one state-aware output control.
Raw protocol evidence available through progressive disclosure.
Motion limited to native direct state feedback.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Teal occupies no more than ten percent of a window and identifies selection, focus, or safe progress only.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Copper and red appear only when an operator decision or a safety condition demands attention.

rules.name: The Exact Number Rule
rules.body: Never replace a measured engineering value with an unlabelled decorative gauge.

rules.name: The Stationary Surface Rule
rules.body: A working instrument stays spatially stable while readings change.

dos: Do keep connection, authentication, freshness, and command outcome visible without opening a dialog.
Do pair every status color with text and a simple symbol.
Do align telemetry decimals and engineering units with the Reading token.
Do keep one output-control location stable while its role follows fresh explicit OFF/ON state.
Do label simulator data as simulated in every relevant surface and export.
Do use familiar native controls and consistent 4–5px shapes.
donts: Don't build a browser or SaaS control panel.
Don't imitate a decorative consumer charging app with gauges that hide exact values.
Don't use a dark “hacker dashboard” with neon accents, glow, or gratuitous motion.
Don't hide automation, reconnect behavior, or uncertain command outcomes.
Don't use color-only alarms or tiny low-contrast telemetry.
Don't expose a raw opcode console capable of transmitting unsupported commands.
Don't invent custom scrollbars, animated gauges, or non-native modal behavior for visual flavor.
